result.topic_en: Riemann's excerpts from James Gregory's 'Vera circuli et hyperbolae quadratura' (1668), giving Gregory's definitions of composed quantities, convergent series and their termination, and from the Commercium epistolicum (1712), quoting Wallis's 1697 letter to Leibniz comparing 'continued approximations', 'convergent series' and 'infinite series'.

methods.what: Gregory's definition of a convergent series: pairs of quantities successively generated from the previous pair by fixed operations, with decreasing differences
methods.quote:
Sint duae quantitates A, B, a quibus componantur duae aliae quantitates C, D, quarum
differentia sit minor differentia quantitatum A, B.

methods.what: Limit ('termination') of a convergent series defined as the common value of the convergent terms when continued to infinity
methods.quote:
possumus imaginari ultimos terminos convergentes esse aequales; quos terminos aequales
appellamus seriei terminationem.

items.quote:
possunt inveniri hujus seriei termini convergentes, quorum differentia sit omni [-quantitate-]
exhibita quantitate minor
items.english: terms of this convergent series can be found whose difference is smaller than any given quantity
For what I had called continued approximations, James Gregory calls convergent series, and Newton infinite series; but the thing is the same.
